_comment: External (non-package-manager) dependencies this codebase tracks pinned versions/commits of. check_dependency_releases.py reads this file and reports when upstream has moved past the pinned point. 'release' mode compares against GitHub's latest-release tag; 'branch' mode compares against a tracked branch's current HEAD commit (used when we deliberately build from a branch other than the default, e.g. a bug fix that only landed on 'develop'). IMPORTANT: 'pinned' means the last version this codebase's own real test suite was actually run against and confirmed working -- not whatever happens to be currently installed/deployed, and never a value copied from a fresh API query without also re-running the tests against it. Bump 'pinned' only after a real verification pass.

kopia.notes: Bumped 2026-08-27 (Bruce: bump all three before deployment). Verified by downloading the real v0.23.1 release tarball, computing its sha256 directly, confirming the archive's internal layout (kopia-0.23.1-linux-x64/kopia) still matches extract_member='kopia', and running the extracted binary (`kopia --version` reports 0.23.1 correctly). No live network-download test exists in this codebase for kopia -- binary_downloader's own test suite mocks urlopen with a self-built tarball -- so this direct download+checksum+run is the real verification pass.

cloudflared.notes: Bumped 2026-09-14 from 2026.8.3 (Bruce: update dependencies when you can), skipping 2026.9.0. Reviewed the real changelog via `gh api repos/cloudflare/cloudflared/compare/2026.8.3...2026.9.1` (14 commits): Go toolchain bump to 1.26.8, removal of upstream's vendor/ directory (build-side only), an access-token lock self-deadlock fix during same-process reauth, edge registration error propagation over QUIC, staged-but-unregistered protected Quick Tunnel plumbing (no new user-reachable flag), and distroless Docker digest bumps. The one potentially breaking item: 2026.9.0 removed the `--transport-loglevel` flag outright, and 2026.9.1 reverted that to deprecated-not-removed (so clients still passing it keep starting) and added a formal 3-month breaking-change notice policy to upstream's README/AGENTS.md. Checked this codebase's real consumer of this manifest entry: it is pager_duty/daemon/generalized_monitor.py, which runs `cloudflared tunnel info <target>` (cloudflare/utils/cloudflare_daemon.py loads the separately vendored libcloudflared.so, not this binary). `grep -rn transport-loglevel` across hams_open (excluding the vendored daemons/cloudflared source) finds no use, and `cloudflared tunnel info --help` on the new binary still documents the same subcommand and positional TUNNEL argument -- so this release is non-breaking for this codebase. Verified the binary itself: downloaded the real 2026.9.1 cloudflared-linux-amd64 release asset (39838488 bytes), computed its sha256 directly (03f1f25d1cc93b9ad6c60569d44060bc4f17ed97075760ed8cfca4b12dcd68cc), which matches both the asset digest GitHub's release API publishes and the checksum list in the release notes, and ran it (`cloudflared --version` reports `2026.9.1 (built 2026-09-11-13:35 UTC)`). Same caveat as kopia/etcd: no live network-download test exists for cloudflared in this codebase, so this direct download+checksum+run is the real verification pass. binary_manifest.json and binary_manifest_data.xml both updated and re-verified in sync via check_binary_manifest_consistency.py. Previous bump, 2026-09-03: dependency-watch.yml surfaced this pin as stale once its own real submodule-checkout bug was fixed (see night_shift_todo.md). 2026.8.3 is a small, low-risk single-version bump whose real changelog (checked via `gh api .../compare`, not assumed) is mostly internal cleanup plus one real security fix: `chore: bump gorilla/websocket for GO-2026-6278` (GHSA-w67g-5rqw-f597, High severity -- a cryptographically weak PRNG in gorilla/websocket's own WebSocket frame-masking, fixed upstream in gorilla/websocket v1.5.3). Verified the same way as the prior bump: downloaded the real 2026.8.3 raw binary release asset, computed its sha256 directly (f29324fe934d1e100617484c78deef803c4dc2cd351d645bbde42e96b4fccc5e, matching the checksum GitHub's own release page publishes for this asset), and ran it (`cloudflared --version` reports `2026.8.3 (built 2026-08-31-10:04 UTC)` correctly). Same caveat as kopia/etcd: no live network-download test exists for cloudflared in this codebase, so this direct download+checksum+run is the real verification pass. binary_manifest.json and binary_manifest_data.xml both updated and re-verified in sync via check_binary_manifest_consistency.py (see that script's own doc comment for the real bug this guards against).

The largest is a real feature, not plumbing: gui_interface/websocket/mongoose.c/.h (28820 lines, GPL-2.0-only, incompatible with Mercury's GPL-3.0-or-later) is replaced by about 1500 lines of Mercury's own RFC 6455 WebSocket server (ws_server.c/.h, ws_frame.c/.h, ws_crypto.c/.h, ws_json.c/.h, and an optional OpenSSL-backed ws_tls.c/.h for wss://). The public API (ws_init, ws_broadcast_json, ws_broadcast_binary, ws_shutdown) is unchanged, so hams_local_relay's own gui_interface/ui_communication.c call sites are untouched, and hams_local_relay never enables Mercury's UI/websocket server in the first place -- spawn_mercury() always passes `-x null` with no `-G`/`-U`, per mercury.rs -- so this whole surface (and the new libssl-dev link dependency it brings when pkg-config finds OpenSSL) is not exercised by the relay at all. Also included: a real safety fix (TX test mode's `-t` loop ignored a first SIGINT/SIGTERM and kept transmitting, needing a second signal and an unclean `_exit()` that could leave PTT keyed -- irrelevant here since the relay never passes `-t`), two i386-only test fixes (a 32-bit PRNG truncation and an x87-vs-SSE float precision assertion, neither reachable on the relay's own x86_64/arm64/armv7 targets), and a Fyne GUI default-host convenience change. No change to CLI flags, the version banner substring, the control-port command set, or `data_interfaces/tcp_interfaces.c` (the file the relay's own loopback-bind patch targets), so both `git apply --check` of that patch and the rigerror2 sed target in install_relay_runtime_deps_rpm.sh still match cleanly. Built for real: cloned mercuryv2 at f8e39359, plain `make`: exit 0 (same 2 pre-existing warnings as every prior bump: snprintf-truncation in cm108_ptt.c, a type-limits comparison in the vendored raptorq ops.c); `-V` prints `Rhizomatica Mercury Version 1.9.14 (git f8e39359)`, matching probe_mercury_installed()'s expected substring; with spawn_mercury()'s exact flags (`-x null -p 19876 -L <log>`) it initialised ARQ, listened on 19876/19877, accepted a real TCP control-port connection, logged it connecting/disconnecting cleanly, and exited 0 on TERM. No datalink_arq change, so upstream's Unity tests were not rerun (matching this file's own established convention for non-ARQ bumps). The relay's own `cargo test mercury` suite was not run locally; every relay CI leg builds mercury at the pinned commit and runs the relay tests against it. Real ARQ deadlock fix, not plumbing: when both ends of a link have a backlog, a MODE_REQ from the floor-holder crossing a TURN_REQ from the other side used to leave both stations retrying to exhaustion -- about 40s of dead air on every such turn (issue #282). TURN_REQ_WAIT now concedes on a crossed MODE_REQ (mirrors the existing RX_DATA concede path); MODE_REQ_WAIT now latches a crossed TURN_REQ in peer_turn_req_pending and hands the floor over on its own MODE_ACK instead of retaining it. hams_local_relay sends no CONNECT/DISCONNECT/MODE_REQ/TURN_REQ itself (mercury.rs only spawns and probes the process; Pat's varahf:// client drives the ARQ protocol), so this only affects how quickly a real two-way session recovers from this specific standoff, not anything the relay's own code calls into. hamlib.pinned_via: hams_com daemons/hams_local_relay/install_relay_runtime_deps.sh HAMLIB_VERSION/HAMLIB_SHA256 (source fallback for building mercury) and hams_com .github/workflows/build-relay.yml build-windows "Cross-build hamlib for mingw-w64" step HAMLIB_VERSION/HAMLIB_SHA256 (statically linked into the Windows binary, plus a native host build whose rigctl/rotctl --list build.rs bakes into its model tables); otherwise the system package (libhamlib-dev), also referenced by hamlib.rs
hamlib.notes: The distro package is used when it provides every Hamlib 4.x call mercury makes (the install script compiles and links a probe to decide). Where it doesn't (Ubuntu 20.04 ships 3.3, Ubuntu 22.04's 4.3.1 lacks rigerror2), install_relay_runtime_deps.sh builds this pinned release from the checksum-verified release tarball as a static library inside its temporary build directory and links mercury against it (added 2026-09-14 after the ubuntu:20.04 CI leg failed with "'RIG_CAPS_PORT_TYPE' undeclared"). When bumping, update HAMLIB_VERSION and HAMLIB_SHA256 there too (sha256 from the release asset's digest: gh api repos/Hamlib/Hamlib/releases/tags/<version>). When bumping, also update build-relay.yml's build-windows step (same two constants): until 2026-09-15 that step downloaded 4.6.2 with no checksum and outside this watch, and baked its model tables from Ubuntu 24.04's libhamlib-utils 4.5.5 rather than the release it links. When bumping, confirm build.rs's fixed-width `rigctl --list` parser still fits the new release's output (the Windows leg's Build log prints "baked N Hamlib rig model(s)").
